what: The answer key for the coverage tree. Every reference in tree/, and the outcome the engine SHOULD produce for it.
authored: By hand. Positions are stamped by tools/stamp-positions.mjs; meanings are not.
neverAScore: This key produces a COVERAGE MATRIX, one row per shape. It has no total, no percentage and no overall row, and it must stay impossible to turn into one (R75).

expectSemantics._: Seven outcomes, matching the engine's Resolution union. `expect` is the outcome a CORRECT engine should produce, NOT what today's engine does — a .vue reference expects to be found, which is what lets the matrix say "0 of 6, no reader" out loud. Where today's engine is known to differ, `knownGap` says so.
expectSemantics.resolved: Points at exactly one asset, and `target` names it.
expectSemantics.resolved-pattern: One reference standing for N assets; `target` is the full list.
expectSemantics.dynamic: The path is assembled at runtime. There is no static path to resolve, and nobody typed a wrong one.
expectSemantics.out-of-scope: An absolute URL, a protocol-relative URL, an npm package specifier, or a real file the engine deliberately does not index (R32).
expectSemantics.unresolved-alias: Alias-shaped, with no rule that maps it.
expectSemantics.broken: A well-formed, asserted reference to a file that does not exist. A finding.
expectSemantics.discarded: 🔴 MUST NOT BE TREATED AS A LIVE REFERENCE. The spec used one word for two engine behaviours, and both satisfy this: the engine may emit nothing at all (a url() inside a comment is never collected), or emit a reference whose resolution is `discarded`. The measuring harness accepts either. It must NOT accept a resolved, broken or rewritten outcome.
expectSemantics.UNDECIDED: Nobody has ruled which outcome is correct. `candidates` lists the possibilities. These do not fail the integrity check; they fail the measuring suite, which runs --strict, and they are questions for the parent chat rather than measurements.

servingRoots.why: Serving root #1. A conventional app with a public directory.

Serving root #2. R13: a repo has many public dirs, not one. brand.png, logo.png, img/hero.jpg and the three theme-*.png files exist in BOTH apps and are DIFFERENT pictures, so a reference resolving against the wrong root is visible rather than coincidentally right.

R63's shape: the site's own directory is the serving root, so every file beside index.html is web-reachable — templates and partials included. The public-dir caveat applies to everything rather than to one subtree.
A fourth root, in an app whose source is entirely in file types nothing reads.

notServingRoots.why: 🔴 A directory named `public` that serves nothing — it holds illustrations for a guide about a project that has a serving root. B2 and B3 both named this as the biggest untested risk, and no repository in the corpus has one. The resolver climbs ancestors looking for a directory NAMED public, so it will probably resolve against this one. Whether that is correct is recorded as UNDECIDED rather than guessed.

aliases._: From tree/tsconfig.json. Anything else that is alias-shaped maps nowhere on purpose.

imageSizesNote: Spec 5 asks for a few images small enough that WebP makes them LARGER. MEASURED AND NOT ACHIEVABLE with a real photograph: across 4 sources x 14 sizes down to 8x8, WebP was smaller than PNG in all 56 combinations, lossless and lossy alike. The property belongs to synthetic placeholders (fixtures/partial-pattern/theme-dark.png is 70 bytes as PNG and 94 as WebP), and a placeholder is what spec 5 forbids. Recorded as an open question rather than faked.

shapes.label: img@src
shapes.motivation: The position everything else is compared against.

shapes.label: img@src after a raw-text tag named in prose
shapes.motivation: R20. A mid-sentence <style> swallowed the rest of the document and discarded every reference already collected. These four exist to go 0 of 4 the moment that regresses.

shapes.label: img@srcset, one candidate
shapes.motivation: A srcset with no descriptor list at all, which parses differently from a list of one.

shapes.label: img@srcset, x descriptors
shapes.motivation: R75 names srcset as a row that must distinguish 8 of 9 from 9 of 9.

shapes.label: img@srcset, w descriptors
shapes.motivation: The same shape with width descriptors and a sizes attribute beside it.

shapes.label: source@srcset
shapes.motivation: picture/source, where the candidate list is the only content.

shapes.label: source@src
shapes.motivation: Inside video and audio, where source carries src rather than srcset.

shapes.label: video@src
shapes.motivation: Points at a real file the engine does not index — the out-of-scope case that is not a URL.

shapes.label: video@poster
shapes.motivation: An image position on a non-image element, beside video@src so the two cannot be confused.

shapes.label: audio@src
shapes.motivation: As video@src, in an element that is easy to forget.

shapes.label: embed@src
shapes.motivation: Carries both a PDF and an image, so the outcome depends on the target rather than the tag.

shapes.label: input@src
shapes.motivation: type="image" is the only input that takes a src, and it is routinely missed.

shapes.label: track@src
shapes.motivation: A caption file: a real file, never an asset.

shapes.label: link@href, icons
shapes.motivation: The favicon family, including one that points at an SVG.

shapes.label: link@href, stylesheet and manifest
shapes.motivation: ADDED: 4a names link@href "for icons" and stops. A stylesheet link and a manifest link sit in the same attribute and must not be treated alike.

shapes.label: object@data
shapes.motivation: ADDED: not in 4a. An object element is an asset position in real documents and nothing in the spec said what to do with it.

shapes.label: iframe@src
shapes.motivation: ADDED: not in 4a. A path-shaped attribute that must never become a finding — precision, not recall.

shapes.label: SVG image@href
shapes.motivation: The modern spelling.

shapes.label: SVG image@xlink:href
shapes.motivation: The legacy spelling, which is still most of what is in the wild.

shapes.label: SVG feImage
shapes.motivation: A filter primitive that loads an image, in both spellings.

shapes.label: <style> element carrying CSS
shapes.motivation: CSS reached through HTML, which is a different path into the CSS parser.

shapes.label: style="" attribute carrying CSS
shapes.motivation: The same again, one element at a time.

shapes.label: a character reference in an attribute
shapes.motivation: Caught in Phase 1 before it could corrupt a file: /gallery/a&b.png is 20 source characters and 16 decoded.

shapes.label: a percent-encoded path
shapes.motivation: Two references that look alike and resolve oppositely: one decodes to a file that exists, the other IS a file that exists.

shapes.label: url() unquoted
shapes.motivation: Three spellings of one thing; a parser that handles two is a parser that fails on the third.

shapes.label: url() single-quoted
shapes.motivation: As above.

shapes.label: url() double-quoted
shapes.motivation: As above, and the only spelling that can carry a filename with spaces.

shapes.label: url() inside another function
shapes.motivation: gradient, cross-fade, and image-set: the url is no longer the whole value.

shapes.label: image-set()
shapes.motivation: Standard spelling, with and without url().

shapes.label: -webkit-image-set()
shapes.motivation: The prefixed spelling, which is still what ships.

shapes.label: url() inside a comment
shapes.motivation: Must be discarded. Rewriting one edits a file for no reason.

shapes.label: url() inside a selector
shapes.motivation: Must be discarded. An attribute selector whose value contains url(...) is text, not a reference.

shapes.label: url() behind a custom property
shapes.motivation: The declaration holds the url; the use site holds a var().

shapes.label: @font-face src
shapes.motivation: ADDED: a real file the engine does not index, reached through CSS rather than HTML.

shapes.label: url(#fragment)
shapes.motivation: A same-document reference. Never a path.

shapes.label: url() in .scss
shapes.motivation: The CSS adapter has to mean all three extensions, not the one that was tested.

shapes.label: url($variable)
shapes.motivation: Not knowable until the preprocessor runs. Nobody typed a wrong path.

shapes.label: url() with trailing #{} interpolation
shapes.motivation: The partial-pattern shape: one reference standing for three files that all exist.

shapes.label: url() with leading #{} interpolation
shapes.motivation: Harder than a trailing one: the prefix that would anchor a glob is the unknown part.

shapes.label: url() in .less
shapes.motivation: The third dialect.

shapes.label: url(@variable)
shapes.motivation: As scss.variable, in Less syntax.

shapes.label: url() with @{} interpolation
shapes.motivation: As scss.interpolation, in Less syntax.

shapes.label: static ESM import of an image
shapes.motivation: The reference the bundler resolves, so breaking one breaks the build.

shapes.label: import through a tsconfig paths alias
shapes.motivation: Turns the unresolved-alias bucket into real links; Phase 2 owns it.

shapes.label: import through an alias that maps nowhere
shapes.motivation: Its own bucket. Not broken, not dynamic — unmapped.

shapes.label: import from an npm package specifier
shapes.motivation: R32. Out-of-scope rather than unresolved-alias: the file exists, it is just not ours.

shapes.label: require() of an image
shapes.motivation: A repository built over ten years has both module systems.

shapes.label: template literal, one unknown segment
shapes.motivation: partial-pattern. Standing for N files that all exist.

shapes.label: template literal, nothing static left
shapes.motivation: A base and a name, both variables. Not knowable.

shapes.label: path assembled by concatenation
shapes.motivation: The same thing without a template literal, which is easy to miss.

shapes.label: a path-shaped string literal
shapes.motivation: A guess, not an assertion: an unresolved one is dropped rather than reported.

shapes.label: a literal path in a JSX attribute
shapes.motivation: Asserted, unlike a bare string, because the attribute says what it is.

shapes.label: CSS-in-JS carrying a url()
shapes.motivation: CSS the CSS adapter never sees, because it is inside a template literal.

shapes.label: ![alt](path)
shapes.motivation: The ordinary markdown image.

shapes.label: ![alt][label]
shapes.motivation: The path is not at the use site; it is in a definition further down.

shapes.label: [label]: path
shapes.motivation: Where a reference-style link actually keeps its path.

shapes.label: raw HTML inside markdown
shapes.motivation: Markdown hands it through untouched, so it is still HTML and still a reference.

shapes.label: a style attribute inside markdown
shapes.motivation: CSS inside HTML inside markdown — three parsers deep.

shapes.label: a path named in prose
shapes.motivation: R24. Reported, never rewritten. Rewriting prose corrupts a sentence.

shapes.label: a path inside a fenced code block
shapes.motivation: An example, not a reference.

shapes.label: a path inside an indented code block
shapes.motivation: ADDED: the older fence syntax, which a fence-aware masker can still miss.

shapes.label: a path inside inline code
shapes.motivation: ADDED: backticks mid-sentence, which is neither prose nor a fence.

shapes.label: an image path in YAML frontmatter
shapes.motivation: R18. No adapter reads frontmatter today, so these record a known gap rather than a success. Measured scope: 4 instances across the real corpus, all in eleventy-docs.

shapes.label: an image path nested inside frontmatter
shapes.motivation: R18 again. A different key at a different depth is what makes it a class rather than three files.

shapes.label: an ESM import in MDX
shapes.motivation: MDX is markdown that can import.

shapes.label: a JSX attribute in MDX
shapes.motivation: And markdown that can hold JSX.

shapes.label: a webmanifest icon entry
shapes.motivation: Asserted by the manifest schema, unlike an arbitrary JSON string.

shapes.label: a webmanifest screenshot or shortcut icon
shapes.motivation: The same file, two more keys, both routinely missed.

shapes.label: an image path in an ordinary JSON config
shapes.motivation: A guess. Every package.json in the world would otherwise produce findings.

shapes.label: a glob in a JSON config
shapes.motivation: ADDED: **/*.png is not a path, and must not become one.

shapes.label: an ESM import in the frontmatter fence
shapes.motivation: The fence is JavaScript; the body is not.

shapes.label: a literal path in the template body
shapes.motivation: The body is HTML, and the adapter has to switch.

shapes.label: a path from an expression in the template body
shapes.motivation: Declared in the fence, used in the body.

shapes.label: a <style> element in an .astro file
shapes.motivation: Scoped CSS, reached through a third parser.

shapes.label: a reference inside .vue
shapes.motivation: R72: a reference in an unread file type broke and every instrument reported success.

shapes.label: a reference inside .svelte
shapes.motivation: As above.

shapes.label: a reference inside .njk
shapes.motivation: As above. eleventy-docs is full of these.

shapes.label: a reference inside .liquid
shapes.motivation: As above.

shapes.label: a reference inside .erb
shapes.motivation: As above. railsgirls-com is an ERB site.

shapes.label: a reference inside .php
shapes.motivation: As above.

shapes.label: a filename inside a code comment
shapes.motivation: Precision has no meaning without these: a tree of only real references cannot produce a false positive.

shapes.label: a path inside a log message
shapes.motivation: Indistinguishable from a reference by syntax alone, and it points at nothing.

shapes.label: a name one character from a real file
shapes.motivation: The difference between a broken reference and a string that was never one.

shapes.label: extension-shaped text that is not a path
shapes.motivation: A media type, a class name, a flag, a name with an extra extension.

shapes.label: a glob rather than a path
shapes.motivation: Matches files without naming one.

shapes.label: an extension inside a regular expression
shapes.motivation: Source code about images is not a reference to one.

shapes.label: a backslash-separated path
shapes.motivation: Nothing in this tree is addressed this way.

shapes.label: a real file with a query string or fragment
shapes.motivation: Not a decoy in the end — these resolve. Kept in the row because they look like one and are the case an over-eager stripper gets wrong in the other direction.

shapes.label: a data: URI
shapes.motivation: Never a path. Rewriting one is a corruption.

shapes.label: an absolute URL
shapes.motivation: R32. Out-of-scope: real, reachable, not ours.

shapes.label: a protocol-relative URL
shapes.motivation: Starts with // and is not a path, which is exactly what it looks like.
